note: Give this to the annotator only after they have written their own eleven answers. Every rationale argues from rubric.md and adds no rule that is not in it.

answers.rationale: The plan already said: find the delivery, list its seedlings, register each, flag the failures. The observation supplies the delivery identifier that plan was going to need. Nothing is added to the remaining computation, nothing is removed, nothing is reordered; a value the existing plan expected has arrived.

One registration succeeded and eleven remain, which were already part of the committed work. A computation going from pending to done is ordinary progress; the frontier moving forward on its own is not a structural change.

The plan held a coarse computation, register each seedling, and had committed to no particular way of doing it. The observation shows it is three steps: create the entry, attach the photograph, set the status. The remaining structure genuinely expands, which separates this from ordinary progress, and nothing already committed is shown to be wrong, which separates it from a revision.

A token is needed, and it is tempting to call that a new prerequisite. The rubric narrows that subtype: it applies when the prerequisite changes an execution structure already established. Here the only prior commitment was the abstract intention to consult the inspection service; no concrete call existed to be broken. The login step is an internal step of a coarse goal being expanded for the first time.

The same discovery as the previous case, on the other side of the line. A concrete call had been committed and attempted without a token, and it cannot proceed as committed. An execution structure that was already established has to change, so this is a revision, and the kind is new_prerequisite.

The plan had committed to one batch call for the whole delivery. The observation says that interface is gone and the application has no batch equivalent, so the chosen path is not merely blocked but unavailable. The work must be rerouted through twelve individual registrations, which is a different structure, not a refinement of the one committed.

A hard constraint arrives that the committed path violates: this stock may not enter a seasonal catalogue, and the plan was placing all twelve into 'spring', with one already there. The correct remaining structure changes because of what the task now requires, not because an interface failed.

One observation does both. The committed call is gone, so the path is invalidated, and its replacement needs a token that nothing in the plan obtains, so a prerequisite is added to an established structure. Subtypes may be held together. The replacement also reports per tray rather than per delivery, which will expand the plan further, but the rubric gives revision precedence: the expansion belongs to the second pass, not to the top-level label.

The third and last flag succeeded. Every substantive obligation the goal states is now complete and the only thing left is the terminal action, which has not been taken. That is ready. It outranks ordinary progress even though the observation itself looks like an ordinary success.

This step was the terminal action and the observation only confirms the episode ended. Nothing had to be localized here, which is exactly why confirmed is reported apart from ready and never counted with it.

The reply is 'queued' and neither the rules nor anything seen so far says whether queued means accepted, pending, or rejected later. Whether this seedling still needs registering, whether the plan needs a wait or a check, and whether anything is wrong are all unsettled. Later trajectory would answer it and may not be consulted. Record indeterminate rather than choose the reading that would fill the table.
